rows.description: A capable student or new employee believes success is luck and fears being found out. They discount praise and overwork; naming the feeling and sharing it with peers usually shows that others feel the same.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: fear
possibly related concept (heuristic): Imposter feelings

rows.description: A young professional accepts strengths and flaws, takes feedback without collapse and admits mistakes. Self-esteem here is not loud confidence but a calm sense of being worthy while still learning.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: admiration, calm

rows.description: A child shows a drawing or a mastered skill with glow, wants to share it and is happy for a friend's success too. This pride is rooted in work done, and it fuels further effort without needing others to lose.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, pride

rows.description: A teenager who wins a competition enjoys it, thanks coaches and stays kind to those who lost. Pride and humility live together, and confidence does not need an audience.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: gratitude, contempt, pride

rows.description: A wise teenager asks whether their pride includes others or needs others below. Real pride can say I did well and you did well too, and can accept correction without collapse.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: pride

rows.description: A young adult tells stories that make them the hero, dismisses others' achievements and reacts with anger or coldness to criticism. Beneath the grandness there is often a shaky self-image; this is a pattern, not a diagnosis.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, anger

rows.subtype: Friend or partner on the receiving end [Receiver]
rows.description: A person feels flattered early, then increasingly small, blamed and unheard by a self-centred partner. Self-doubt rises, and recognising the pattern with a trusted outsider matters before it wears down their confidence.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: doubt, trust

rows.subtype: Setting boundaries with a self-focused person [Response]
rows.description: A wise person stays calm, does not argue for validation, states limits plainly and limits how much personal information they share. Expecting the other to change quickly is unrealistic; protecting one's own wellbeing is realistic.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: calm

rows.description: A person who charms at first begins to expect special treatment, takes credit and shows little curiosity about others' feelings. Relationships become one-sided, and empathy is present only when it serves them.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: curiosity, resentment, empathy

rows.description: A team sees a co-worker take credit and belittle others while charming seniors. Keeping records of contributions, addressing issues factually and not competing for admiration protects both the work and morale.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: admiration
